findings.description: r0's major is closed, not restated. T-002's check_method now runs the consumer suite and requires exit 0, citing C-16, and the fix lands the attribution where r0 said it had to land: at check time for the task that made the edit, before T-004's worker ever opens the file.
findings.evidence: T-002.md:23-28 adds "Consumer suite, per C-16: this task edits prose the smoke suite pins verbatim, so run `bash tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` and require exit 0," with the attribution reasoning attached. The excerpt gains a "Two sentences the suite pins verbatim" section at T-002.md:67-78 quoting both assertions with correct line numbers — verified: `sed -n '524p'` is `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "one sanctioned exception to preserving raw content"` and `sed -n '554p'` is `require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "**Five body reads per input, and the budget binds.**"`. `grep -c 'inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md' tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` still returns 27. T-002.md:78 grants the permission the r0 finding implied was missing — "You may reword either — but if you do, update its assertion in the same breath, and keep the assertion pinning something load-bearing rather than softening it to a substring that would survive anything" — which is the right shape, because C-10 may genuinely require rewording the VTT bullet at SKILL.md:459. Attribution is clean at this point in the graph: T-002 deps only on T-001, whose deliverable is an untracked script no suite invokes until T-004 lands, so any suite failure at T-002's check time is T-002's. One residual is filed as a minor below.

findings.description: r0's second major is closed by the first of the two options offered. T-003 deps are now [T-002, T-005], the DAG is still acyclic, and the excerpt tells the worker in the terms the finding asked for that C-11's question 2 has already flipped for the EVALS.md passage.
findings.evidence: T-003.md:26 `deps: [T-002, T-005]`. New excerpt section at T-003.md:69-73, "EVALS.md is in your census, and it moved before you got here": it states the eight-hit count, names `:34` as the live hit, and closes with "T-005's new scenario changes the answer to question 2 — before it shipped, `:34` was the document's only account of the gate; now the new scenario has its own. Read the file as it stands, not as the census list describes it." Both facts re-derived: the sweep returns exactly 8 hits in `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md` (`:11, :34, :38, :48, :49, :52, :56, :58`), and `:34` reads "Phase 5 is gated, so a scenario that grades a crystallized record needs you to approve the candidates it names at the sign-off prompt, and only those" — the only one of the eight that is an account of the gate rather than scenario-1 content. The last sentence is the load-bearing one: it stops the worker grading a document state the census list describes, and it does not pre-decide the outcome, which the clause reserves for the two questions. The deps edge is also the only instrument available here — I checked for a consumer suite and there is none: `grep -rn 'EVALS' tests/` returns one hit, `tests/file-issue-smoke.sh:47`, against a different skill's file.

findings.description: r0's third major is closed. The unsatisfiable whole-tree assertion is replaced with one a checker-deterministic can actually run against a single file, and the task now says in as many words why whole-tree scope is not its job.
findings.evidence: T-006.md:15-19: "Then confirm the edit stayed in its lane: `git diff -- _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/eval-scope.sh` touches only the header comment block at :1-9 and no executable line. Do not attempt to confirm the repo-wide diff — five tasks have already landed and git carries no per-task attribution; whole-tree scope is C-16's, owned by T-007." That is satisfiable: the file has exactly one owner (`_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/eval-scope.sh` appears in no other task's surface, and T-005.md:75 excludes it by name), so the path-scoped diff carries this task's edit and nothing else. The structure holds — `sed -n '1,14p'` shows the shebang at `:1`, the comment block through `:9` with the citation on `:6`, and `set -euo pipefail` at `:10`, so "no executable line" is a real boundary with a real first violation. The pointer back to C-16/T-007 also fixes the derivation problem r0 named: the sentence no longer reads as if C-15 asserted something about diff scope. One residual about the literal range is filed as a minor below.

findings.description: r0's routing minor is closed. worker-bulk/haiku to worker-standard/sonnet is the rung the routing table's own description picks for this work, and the excerpt now says why in the task itself.
findings.evidence: T-006.md:6-8 `executor: worker-standard` / `executor_model: sonnet` / `checker: checker-deterministic`. T-006.md:53 adds "This is a prose edit, not a substitution. The sentence has to still read as the aside it is, so do not mechanically swap the number for a quoted string and leave the grammar behind it broken." The table gives sonnet "Clear-spec implementation judged on correctness," and this task is clear-spec — T-006.md:41 enumerates the acceptable forms ("point at the rule by what it says, or by the guard's variable, or by naming the section") and T-006.md:47-51 hands the worker its own verification command. I considered worker-craft and rejected it: the table reserves opus for "User-facing/taste work," and a header comment inside a `_maintenance/` staging script is neither. Checker stays checker-deterministic and that is still right — C-15's check is a grep plus resolving each hit against the cited line, and I re-ran the sweep: `grep -rnoE 'inbox-to-memory-smoke\.sh:[0-9]+' _maintenance/ inbox-to-memory/ tests/` returns exactly one hit, `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/eval-scope.sh:6`, so there is one thing to resolve and it is mechanical.

findings.description: r0's stale-line-number minor is closed, and closed better than the one word I suggested. The excerpt now voids every number in the placement section up front and hands the worker a single command that re-derives both guard anchors.
findings.evidence: T-004.md:46: "Every line number in this section was read off the suite **before T-002 ran**, and T-002 inserted a line near `:300`. Re-derive them; do not trust them. `/usr/bin/grep -n 'fixtures_before' tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` gives you both guard anchors in one call." I ran that grep: it returns `586:fixtures_before="$(find ...)"` and `1299:[[ "$(find ...)" == "$fixtures_before" ]] || {`, both anchors, one call, exactly as claimed — and dropping the `=` from C-13's own `fixtures_before=` pattern is what makes one call cover both. The disclaimer's scope is right: it opens the "Placement, and why it is fussy" section, which is where all four affected anchors live (`:586`, `:1299`, the `:1296-1298` guard comment at T-004.md:56, and the `:1227` banner style at T-004.md:52). Those all still resolve against the tree today — `:1296` opens "# The checked-in fixtures are never migrated in place." and `:1227` is "# v1 link checking (#32)" — so the worker starts from correct numbers and is told they will have moved.

findings.description: r0's bracket-sensitivity minor is closed in both places, and the warning as written is technically exact rather than approximately right, including the escape hatch.
findings.evidence: T-002.md:84 and T-003.md:83 carry near-identical paragraphs: the extraction greps `\[[a-z][a-z0-9 -]*(:|\])`, "which catches any bracketed run of lowercase letters, digits, spaces, and hyphens — not only tokens. It already picks up `[target]` from the existing text. So a new markdown link with an all-lowercase label, or a bracketed aside like `[see below]`, registers as a token shape and fails a clause in someone else's task. Existing link labels carrying `/` or `.` are safe." Every part re-derived. I ran C-12's `inv()` at the working tree: it returns 14 entries and `[target]` is one of them. The `/`-and-`.` escape hatch is correct against the pattern — the character class admits only `[a-z0-9 -]`, so `[see docs/foo]` never reaches a `:` or `]` and produces no match, and a capitalized first letter fails `[a-z]` outright. Both tasks also correctly name the check as running in someone else's task, which is the part that makes the warning act on a worker who will not be there to defend the edit.

findings.description: Asked whether T-003 now owning EVALS.md changes the ruling on `_memory.template.md` as a shared contract: it does not. Leave it as filed. The reasoning that held it to a minor is about reachability, and reachability did not change.
findings.evidence: The r0 argument stands unaltered: `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh:374-376` loops `for scaffold in notes journal _memory` and asserts `require_text "inbox-to-memory/assets/claude-md/$scaffold.template.md" "schema: 2"`, and C-11's obligation on that file (constitution.md:397, "accounts for the write-through *somewhere in the document*") is additive narrative that cannot delete a `schema: 2` line from the required-frontmatter block. T-003 acquiring EVALS.md does not put a second pinned string in reach in that file. What it does do is put a *different* set of pinned strings in reach one file over — C-14's four enumeration greps in EVALS.md — and that is where the residual now lives. Filed as a minor below rather than as a second consumer-suite citation, because the instrument does not fit: EVALS.md has no consuming suite (`grep -rn 'EVALS' tests/` finds only the unrelated `file-issue` one), so a `bash tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` line in T-003's check_method would not check the thing at risk. One Out-of-scope sentence would.

findings.description: Re-checked with T-003's new edge. The graph is still a DAG, every referenced id resolves, and the new edge did not create the one thing worth fearing — a path that makes T-003 and T-004 mutually ordered when they touch disjoint files.
findings.evidence: Parsed all seven `deps` lists and ran a colored DFS: T-001 [] ; T-002 [T-001] ; T-003 [T-002, T-005] ; T-004 [T-001, T-002] ; T-005 [T-002] ; T-006 [T-004] ; T-007 [T-001..T-006]. No cycle reported, no missing id, topological order T-001, T-002, T-005, T-003, T-004, T-006, T-007. The new edge T-003 -> T-005 is safe because T-005's only dep is T-002, which T-003 already had: it adds one arc into an existing chain rather than joining two branches, so it cannot close a loop. Parallelism is preserved where it matters — T-003 and T-004 remain unordered siblings, and they touch disjoint files (T-003 works `inbox-to-memory/` and `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/`; T-004 works `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh`). The one edge r0 called over-constrained-but-harmless, T-006 on T-004, is unchanged and still worth keeping for the reason r0 gave.

findings.description: Built the file-to-task write map explicitly from each task's body rather than from its title, as asked. Three files have two owners; all three are now ordered by a dep edge. There is a fourth multi-owner file the map turns up, and it is a different shape — filed as a minor below rather than as a repeat of the r0 pattern.
findings.evidence: The map: T-001 -> `inbox-to-memory/scripts/stamp-confirmed.sh` (create). T-002 -> `inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md`, `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` (the `:300` line, plus conditionally the `:524`/`:554` assertions). T-003 -> whatever the census condemns under `inbox-to-memory/` and `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/`, concretely `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `references/machine-contracts.md`, `references/migration.md`, `references/retrieval-funnel.md`, `assets/claude-md/*.template.md`, `assets/readme/*.template.md`, `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md`. T-004 -> `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh`. T-005 -> `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/EVALS.md`, `tests/fixtures/inbox-to-memory/evals/confirmation-writethrough/` (create). T-006 -> `_maintenance/inbox-to-memory/eval-scope.sh`. T-007 -> nothing by default. Two owners: (1) `SKILL.md` — T-002, T-003, ordered; (2) `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` — T-002, T-004, ordered, and their regions do not even overlap since T-002 works at `:300`/`:524`/`:554` and T-004's section goes between `:586` and `:1299`; (3) `EVALS.md` — T-003, T-005, now ordered, the r1 fix. The fourth is `stamp-confirmed.sh`: T-001 authors it and T-003's census sweep will hit it repeatedly once it exists, since the sweep's predicate includes the bare word `last_confirmed`. It is ordered, so there is no write race — the exposure is that T-003 has no instruction to leave it alone. Filed below. Nothing else doubles up: `eval-scope.sh` produces zero sweep hits today (the per-file count is EVALS.md 8, and eval-scope.sh 0), so T-003 and T-006 do not collide, and the new evals fixture sits under `tests/fixtures/`, outside the census scope entirely.

findings.description: The challenge asked for, ruled: keep T-003 last. Running the census against the finished tree is the only ordering under which its verdict is stable, and the cost the orchestrator worried about — stale line numbers — is the cheap half of the problem and already handled. The expensive half is churn, and that is what the T-003 minor below is about.
findings.evidence: Three reasons to keep it. First, C-11's question 2 is document-state-dependent by construction — "is this passage its document's only account" — so a census run early produces rulings that other tasks then invalidate, and nothing in the lifecycle re-opens a `complete` task to re-derive them. The retry ladder is for FAILs, not for re-verification. Second, the constitution is explicit that everything is "measured against the shipped tree, not against a worker's account of it" (constitution.md:12), and the checker re-derives the sweep at check time (T-003.md:10-11) — so a check run against a mid-job tree is checking a tree that will not ship. Third, the run-early-verify-late alternative means splitting C-11 across two dispatches with two checkers, which is precisely the functional clause split the r0 CLAUSE-OWNERSHIP pass went looking for and did not find; it would trade a documented minor for a structural defect. On the stale-number worry specifically: the floor list at T-003.md:65 is a list of *passages*, and the sweep re-derives them by content (T-003.md:60-63), so a shifted number costs the worker a re-grep and nothing else — T-003.md:65 already says "Line numbers will have shifted in SKILL.md since T-002." I re-ran the sweep to confirm the floor is still a floor: SKILL.md returns 10 hits (`:26, :57, :79, :138, :168, :353, :361, :392, :423, :455`) against the five the floor names, so the "floor, not a boundary" framing is doing real work.

findings.description: The blast-radius enumeration undercounts. Five of the suite's 27 SKILL.md assertions pin strings inside the four sections T-002 is ordered to rewrite, not two — and the reword permission at T-002.md:78 is scoped to "either" of the two the excerpt names, which could read to a worker as a closed list.
findings.evidence: Resolved every pinned string to its SKILL.md line and cross-referenced against the section ranges (`grep -nE '^#{2,3} '`): phase 2.5 is `:53-80`, phase 6 is `:170-191`, Operating Rules is `:450-462`. In range: suite `:540` pins `"### Phase 2.5 — Check Against Accepted Memory"` (SKILL.md:53, the heading of a section this task rewrites); suite `:551` pins the alias-table sentence at SKILL.md:62; suite `:554` pins SKILL.md:67 (named); suite `:555` pins `"read budget bound is named"` at SKILL.md:186, inside phase 6, which C-9 tells this worker to rewrite; suite `:524` pins SKILL.md:459 (named). The `:541-547` loop additionally pins the phase 4, 5 and 6 headings, which bracket the insertion point C-17 specifies. Why this stays minor rather than reopening the major: the check_method's suite run catches a break in any of the five, at T-002's own check, with clean attribution — which is the whole of what r0 asked for, and it does not depend on the excerpt enumerating correctly. T-002.md:78 also ends "Run `bash tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh` before you report done; it is part of your check," so the worker discovers the other three the same way the checker would. The one-line close: replace "You may reword either" with a general permission — you may update any assertion your edits break, on the same terms — and add `:540` and `:555` to the quoted block, since T-002.md:39's "add one line to `tests/inbox-to-memory-smoke.sh`" plus T-002.md:65's "One line" could otherwise read as forbidding the fix the worker needs.

findings.description: The census sweep reaches three shell scripts and T-003 excludes exactly one of them by name. The two it misses are the two with consequences: `lint-scope.sh`, a frozen non-goal deliberately outside C-16's allowlist, and T-001's `stamp-confirmed.sh`, another task's deliverable that is inside it.
findings.evidence: The sweep is `grep -rniE "sign-?off|auto-promote|automatic|per-candidate|approval|last_confirmed" inbox-to-memory/ _maintenance/inbox-to-memory/`, and I ran it: `inbox-to-memory/scripts/migrate-scope.sh` 3 hits, `inbox-to-memory/scripts/lint-scope.sh` 1 hit. `stamp-confirmed.sh` does not exist yet but will match `last_confirmed` on most of its lines once T-001 ships, and T-003 runs after it. T-003.md:77 handles only the first: "`inbox-to-memory/scripts/migrate-scope.sh:348-349` ... **Do not fix it** — that file is frozen for this job. Surface it in your notes as a finding." The asymmetric consequences are what make this worth recording. An edit to `lint-scope.sh` fails C-16 at T-007 — constitution.md:587 keeps it off the allowlist on purpose, "the second lock on the no-lint-changes non-goal" — and T-007.md:68 tells that worker to report rather than revert, so the job ends at its last task with a finding pointing back at a task already marked `complete`. An edit to `stamp-confirmed.sh` is worse in a quieter way: constitution.md:579 admits it to the allowlist by filename, so check-diff-scope.py passes it, and the only thing that would notice is C-13's suite run inside T-007. Why it is still a minor: C-11's text is scoped to "the skill's own **prose**" (constitution.md:394), T-003's whole framing is passages a reader reads, and the migrate-scope.sh precedent teaches surface-do-not-fix. The close is one sentence extending T-003.md:77 to all of `inbox-to-memory/scripts/` — none of it is prose, and every file in it belongs to another task or to a non-goal.

findings.description: T-003 now writes into EVALS.md after T-005 is marked complete, and C-14's four enumeration greps are the thing at risk. T-003's check_method runs no suite and no clause re-checks those greps afterwards — the same shape as the r0 T-002 finding, one file over, at much lower probability.
findings.evidence: C-14's mechanical block (constitution.md:540-543) pins four things in EVALS.md: `grep -c '^Four, all under'` must be 0, `'^Five, all under'` must be 1, `confirmation-writethrough` must appear, and `grep -c '^| [0-9]\.'` must be 5. T-005's checker verifies those and the task goes `complete`; T-003 then edits the same file, and neither T-007's clauses (C-12, C-16) nor any suite touches EVALS.md — confirmed, `grep -rn 'EVALS' tests/` returns only `tests/file-issue-smoke.sh:47`. So a T-003 edit that added a numbered table row or touched `:9` would silently un-satisfy a clause already passed. Probability is low and that is why this is minor: T-003's obligation is `:34`, a prose sentence in the how-to-run section, 90-odd lines from the Grading table, and C-14's greps are content-anchored rather than line-anchored so an insertion elsewhere is invisible to them. The same paragraph should also mention SKILL.md:423, the one census hit in T-003's own floor that the suite pins verbatim (`require_text inbox-to-memory/SKILL.md "$record_key_order"` at suite `:316`) — C-11's two questions dismiss it on sight, since a bare key-order list makes no claim about when writes happen, but the worker has no way to know it is pinned. Close both with one Out-of-scope sentence: EVALS.md's four enumerations are T-005's and are pinned by C-14; SKILL.md's key-order line is pinned by the suite; your edits are prose and must not reach either.

findings.description: The replacement assertion bounds the diff with a line range the edit itself is likely to extend. Narrow, and ironic in the one task whose entire subject is that a line number is not an anchor.
findings.evidence: T-006.md:16-17 asks the checker to confirm the diff "touches only the header comment block at :1-9 and no executable line," and T-006.md:57 repeats "your diff stays inside the header comment block at `:1-9`." The block is `:1-9` today with `set -euo pipefail` at `:10`, verified. But the task's own instruction is to replace a nine-character citation with a descriptive form — T-006.md:41, "point at the rule by what it says, or by the guard's variable, or by naming the section" — and at the file's ~78-column comment wrapping that plausibly adds a line, putting `set -euo pipefail` at `:11` and the block at `:1-10`. A checker-deterministic applying `:1-9` literally then FAILs a correct artifact, which is the failure mode r0 filed against the old sentence, surviving in miniature. Two things hold it to minor: the clause is C-15, the document's only minor-severity clause, and the second half of the same sentence — "and no executable line" — is the operative test and is stable, so a checker with any latitude reads through to it. The close is to drop the range and keep the property: the diff touches only comment lines above `set -euo pipefail`, and no executable line.

findings.description: Re-derived rather than carried forward, because r1 added a clause citation to a check_method. All eighteen clauses are still owned by exactly one task, and T-002's C-16 reference did not leak ownership.
findings.evidence: Parsed every task's `clauses` list: T-001 [C-1..C-7, C-18] = 8, T-002 [C-8, C-9, C-10, C-17] = 4, T-003 [C-11], T-004 [C-13], T-005 [C-14], T-006 [C-15], T-007 [C-12, C-16]. Total 18, unique 18, no gaps against C-1..C-18, no duplicates. The thing to check here was T-002: its check_method now says "Consumer suite, per C-16" while `clauses` stays `[C-8, C-9, C-10, C-17]`, which is the right construction and the one the orchestrator intended. C-16 remains T-007's to own and to fail on; T-002 borrows its check as a gate on its own artifact, which is what the decompose skill's shared-contract rule asks for — it says the task "cites the constitution's consumer-suite clause in its `check_method`," not in its clause list. The distinction matters because T-002's checker cannot pass or fail C-16 for the tree; it can only refuse to pass T-002 while the suite is red.

findings.description: Re-derived for the one task r1 re-tiered. All seven assignments now follow the table, which is a change from r0's six of seven.
findings.evidence: T-001 worker-standard/sonnet + checker-deterministic (eight clauses, all runnable bash, no rubric). T-002, T-003, T-005 worker-craft/opus + checker-judgment (C-8, C-9, C-10, C-11, C-14 each literally open `checker-judgment:`). No dispatch-guard mismatch: every `executor_model` matches its `executor`'s tier in the table — sonnet for worker-standard, opus for worker-craft, and no worker-bulk left in the set.

findings.description: The tree is as the dispatch describes it and as T-007's excerpt claims, and I left it that way. No file outside `.agent-guild/state/verdicts/` was written by this audit.
findings.evidence: `git status --porcelain | wc -l` returns 18, and every path is under `.agent-guild/state/archive/*/tasks/` across five archive directories (`2026-08-06`, `2026-08-07`, `2026-08-07-issue-29`, `2026-08-08-issue-17`, `2026-08-08-issue-32`). `inbox-to-memory/`, `tests/`, and `_maintenance/` are clean. T-007.md:70-72's "One thing that is not a finding" is accurate against that, and its claim that the `.agent-guild/` allowlist entry admits them matches constitution.md:584. Every command this audit ran was a read: grep, sed, wc, git status, git show, and a python parse of the task frontmatter. C-12's `inv()` was run read-only against the working tree and the base commit.
